1#main: The measure of the margin and spacing between line and line and between page and page. In it are 6 seifim. The measure of the margin below is four fingerbreadths in size; and above, three; and between each page and page, two. Therefore one must leave at the beginning and end of each sheet the width of a finger, and space for sewing; and it is found that when the sheets are sewn together there will be between each page and page in the entire book the width of two fingerbreadths. And between line and line—as the full width of a line. And between each chumash and chumash—four blank lines without writing, and one begins the chumash from the beginning of the fifth line. And one leaves at its beginning and end enough to roll on the pole, and also the two fingerbreadths that remain between the pole and the page.
2#main: One should not diminish the writing because of the space below and above, nor because of the space between parashah and parashah.
3#main: If a five-letter word came to him, he should not write two inside the page and three outside the page, but rather write three inside the page and two outside the page. And if there is no room to write three inside the page, he leaves the place partly empty and does not stretch the letters to make them larger than their fellows in order to fill to the end of the page (Hagahos Maimoniyos in the name of the Rambach). And a three-letter word—one may write two of it outside the page even though most of it is inside; but if it has only two letters, one does not write them outside the page. {Rama: And even if the two letters are from a large word and appear like a word by themselves, one does not write them on the margin (Beit Yosef in the name of Mordechai, who so wrote in the name of Semak).}
4#main: If a ten-letter word came to him, or less or more, and not enough remains on the line to write all of it inside the page—if he can write half inside the page and half outside the page, he writes; and if not, he leaves the place empty and begins from the beginning of the line.
5#main: All these matters are only for the optimal mitzvah; and if one changed, it is valid.
6#main: If he forgot to write the entire Name, he hangs it between the lines; but part of the Name on the line and part hanging is invalid. And in other words, if he forgot—he writes part of the word on the line and part above. {Rama: Some scribes are meticulous to write yud-hei shin-mem-vav at the tops of the columns, and some meticulous ones write vav at the top of each column and call it vavei ha'amudim. And one need not be meticulous in all this; and even the more meticulous should not diminish or expand the writing at times because of this (Hagahos Maimoniyos chapter 7), for all these matters have no root on which to rely (Beit Yosef).} (°)
